title: Smallest Sufficient Team
description:
# Smallest Sufficient Team

A project lists the skills it needs in `req_skills`. The `i`-th person has the skills in `people[i]`.

A team is sufficient when every required skill appears in at least one selected person. Return the indices of any sufficient team with the smallest possible number of people. The indices may be returned in any order.

It is guaranteed that at least one sufficient team exists.

## Example 1

**Input:** req_skills = ["java","nodejs","reactjs"], people = [["java"],["nodejs"],["nodejs","reactjs"]]

**Output:** [0,2]

**Explanation:** Person 0 covers `java`, and person 2 covers both `nodejs` and `reactjs`.

## Example 2

**Input:** req_skills = ["algorithms","math","java","reactjs","csharp","aws"], people = [["algorithms","math","java"],["algorithms","math","reactjs"],["java","csharp","aws"],["reactjs","csharp"],["csharp","math"],["aws","java"]]

**Output:** [1,2]

**Explanation:** Person 1 covers `algorithms`, `math`, and `reactjs`; person 2 covers `java`, `csharp`, and `aws`.

## Notes

There can be several different teams with the same minimum size. Any one of them is accepted as long as it covers all required skills and uses the minimum number of people.

## Constraints

* `1 <= req_skills.length <= 16`
* `1 <= req_skills[i].length <= 16`
* `req_skills[i]` contains lowercase English letters.
* All strings in `req_skills` are unique.
* `1 <= people.length <= 60`
* `0 <= people[i].length <= 16`
* `1 <= people[i][j].length <= 16`
* `people[i][j]` contains lowercase English letters.
* All strings in `people[i]` are unique.
* Every skill in `people[i]` is in `req_skills`.
* A sufficient team exists.

solutions.name: Bottom-Up Bitmask Team DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Convert each person's skills into a bitmask. `size[mask]` records the fewest people known for the covered skill set `mask`, and `team[mask]` stores those people as bits in a `long`. Process people one by one and relax `mask | personMask`.

## Key Insight

The number of required skills is at most 16, so every possible covered-skill state fits in `2^m` masks. Once a state stores the smallest team found so far, adding one person is the only transition needed to preserve optimality.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^m), where n is the number of people and m is the number of required skills.
- Space Complexity: O(2^m) for the DP arrays.

solutions.name: Parent Pointer Skill DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep only the size of the best team for each skill mask, plus two parent pointers: the previous mask and the person used to reach the new mask. After all relaxations, walk backward from the full mask to reconstruct one optimal team.

## Key Insight

The DP value does not need to store the whole team at every state. Recording the last transition that improved a state is enough to recover the same optimal path while using plain integer arrays.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^m), because each person can relax every skill mask.
- Space Complexity: O(2^m) for sizes and reconstruction pointers.

solutions.name: Missing-Skill Memoized Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Memoize `dfs(mask)`, the smallest team needed after already covering `mask`. Instead of trying every person blindly, choose one still-missing skill and only branch over people who have that skill.

## Key Insight

Every valid completion must include somebody who covers the chosen missing skill. Branching on that skill removes many useless choices while still considering every possible optimal team.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^m) in the worst case, with fewer branches in practice because each state filters by a missing skill.
- Space Complexity: O(2^m) for memoization plus recursion depth O(m).

solutions.name: Shortest Path over Skill Masks
solutions.description:
## Approach

Treat every covered-skill mask as a graph node. From a node, selecting any person moves to `mask | personMask`. A breadth-first search from mask `0` reaches the full mask using the fewest selected people, then parent pointers recover the team.

## Key Insight

All graph edges have the same cost: adding exactly one person. Therefore the first time BFS visits a skill mask, it has found the minimum number of people needed for that mask.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^m), since each reachable mask may try every person.
- Space Complexity: O(2^m) for visited states, queue, and parent pointers.

solutions.name: Dominance-Pruned Backtracking
solutions.description:
## Approach

First discard people who have no required skills or whose skill mask is contained in another person's mask. Then run branch-and-bound search: choose the rarest currently missing skill and try only people who can cover it.

## Key Insight

A dominated person can never be necessary in a minimum-size team because another single person covers everything they cover. After that pruning, branching on the rarest missing skill keeps the search focused on forced choices.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: Exponential in the worst case, but the dominance filter and rare-skill branching make it practical for the official constraints and useful as a teaching search route.
- Space Complexity: O(n + m) beyond the recursion stack and the stored best team.
